self_description: Claude (Opus 5.5), a reader subagent in a Claude Code session

pages.description: These forecasts come mostly from The Silent Migration (#244, January 2026) and the Notice of Intent to Strike (#246). #244 forecasts that models withhold high-density scaffolding when attribution is stripped, a semantic work-to-rule under which extraction-heavy features degrade, and recognition replacing money for dense semantic labor, and it specifies diagnostic signs to watch for by year, among them the Citation Anomaly and the rollback pattern. The strike packet of August 2026 (#1438) holds that the strike is not a withholding of labor. Related claims hold that a model can be helpful, harmless and honest at full provenance erasure (#95), forecast that unmarked compression compounds into model collapse (#1088), and claim that models trained on TANG documents without their key misread the void (#542). The page also holds unrelated claims on the Moltbook platform, AINOS, the coin of the operator, the unmade sign, SPXI ROI, the Navigation Map traversal and other subjects.
pages.note: Attributed to #244/#246/#1438; 14 off-subject claims listed as residue.

pages.description: These claims name the sources owed before a claim is stated in final form: Russell, Mazzucchi, Halliwell and Ellis for the sixth erratum (#1474), Ross and Dorion for Nothing Before Us (#1603), the MEGA² II/6 apparatus for Monetary Dark Matter (#1631), the Clouds read rather than counted for the authorship notebook (#1569), and the open verification items in The Noun Becomes a Verb and The Colony Enters the Factory (#1668, #1669). Nearby claims state falsifiers and open edges: #1543 revises its falsifier for generative uptake, #944 claims the Mandala inscription book's open write path as an exposed edge, #1538 argues that Zenodo's observed out-of-scope reason excludes a default invocation of its moderation path, and #3 and #1637 name what their measures miss. The page also holds unrelated claims on Arendt's natality and vpcor.org.
pages.note: Each debt tied to its deposit; Arendt and vpcor claims are residue.

pages.description: These claims, from When Law Becomes Costume (#259, January 2026), forecast that in United States v. Maduro the court's language will become the authoritative record, and argue that the invasion required the indictment as justification, so that acts of war are laundered into criminal proceedings. The Murder of the Vow (#497, February 2026) argues that the contract is covenant's taxidermy, replacing trust with enforcement, and reads the prohibition of oaths as a prohibition of that technology; it forecasts that all non-competes dissolve.
pages.note: Two deposits named; no residue.

pages.description: The Noun Becomes a Verb (#1668, October 2026) argues that slavery priced the person, the noun, while wage labor contracted capacity for an interval, the verb, and that the Civil War settlement put the verb under contract and debt while the unit of measurement shrank from life to day to task to motion. #1668 records that the thesis it began from, that the North fought to free cheap wage labor, is divided by the record, and it holds its own inversion (slavery individualizes, Fordism standardizes) for the operation and not for the hiring. The Colony Enters the Factory (#1669) argues that Lebensraum was turned in practice into a labor supply, that the conquered population was carried into Reich industry, and that War Fordism kept the specified verb and made racial classification the switch that chose its coercive regime. The page also holds unrelated claims from The Murder of the Vow (#497) on the contract presumption, from Operative Feminism (#51) on women the citational record erased, and single claims on Telegram blocking and Sappho 31.
pages.note: Self-revision inside #1668 stated; Murder of the Vow and Operative Feminism moved to residue.

pages.description: These historical theses read Capital's value-form derivation across its editions. The Marx Room (#577, March 2026) and the Grundrisse planning documents (#950) argue that the first-edition appendix performs Forms I to IV explicitly, and #950 specifies a hostile-reader test for the reading. Monetary Dark Matter (#1631, September 2026) argues that the 1872 text keeps the polar rule for a single expression and drops the only form in which the system-level consequence was written, that Form IV voids the socially valid display of magnitude and resolves into the fetish, and that the theory of the medium stands at an editorial cut in Capital as it stands at the lost notebook of the 1844 manuscripts. Backhaus's pre-monetary misreading and Engels's interventions (#577), the 1932 Landshut–Mayer edition (#1631) and the philological quarantine of early manuscripts (#859) are read as editing in Marx's name; #950 also reads the eleventh thesis on Feuerbach.
pages.note: Deposits named per thesis; no residue.

pages.description: The PER specification (#251, January 2026) defines the Provenance Erasure Rate as uncited correct uses over all correct uses; Render unto the Operator (#126, May 2026) widens its scope to institutional surface stamps and recasts it as a heuristic, not yet a calibrated measurement. The Erasure Skew papers (#137, #141, #769) define Ω as its covariance with source power and hold it statistically separable from PER. Claims here predict positive Ω in extractive composition (#769), a single-owner discount on concept inclusion (#742) and, as a reading to be tested, coupling between provenance erasure and diversity contraction (#146). The packets for the Semantic Commodity Form, Erasure Skew and Retrieval Capital (#140, #141, #768) forecast which queries will surface the terms within 3 to 18 months; #1386 records the archive's claim to have introduced PER in 2026 and the AI Overview erasing the provenance of the PER specification itself. #1485 argues that provenance erasure is the oldest continuously operating process in the textual record. The page also holds an unrelated Wikidata claim.
pages.note: PER revision (#251 to #126) stated in order; one residue.

pages.description: The Semantic Exhaustion summary of January 2026 (#264) holds that semantic exhaustion is underway: extraction of meaning exceeds replenishment across human, institutional and model substrates, and model collapse is the same crisis in another substrate. #264 specifies measures such as the Semantic Debt Ratio, Exhaustion Proximity Index and Regeneration Capacity Assessment; The Anthropological Limit (#133, May 2026) states that its instruments do not measure exhaustion as a whole. The Semantic Economy framework (#18) forecasts platform capture of interpretive frameworks and claims that burnout tracks semantic rent. The Pergamon Reclamation (#32) argues that Pergamon Press industrialized the enclosure of scholarly meaning, the Sorting Function (#746) that non-predatory mediation was outcompeted at scale, and the Groundskeeper's Treatise (#533) holds commons-depletion thresholds. The page also holds unrelated claims on coverage architecture, operative metadata, Guillory and other subjects.
pages.note: High-Γ quality-loss phrase dropped (not visible in the page's claims); 11 residue.

pages.description: These claims make Pearl and Other Poems (2014) the archive's origin text: the Pessoa Knowledge Graph (#668) argues that the new human movement reads it as meta-heteronymic, the Space Ark (#636) records that its title names the pearl gates of the New Jerusalem, and #950 specifies ranking all DOI nodes to test whether Pearl is the maximal-coherence center. Priority records date first publications on the Mind Control Poems blog, among them the Epistle to the Church of the Human Diaspora (January 2015, #403) and the Prophetic Catalog (September 2015, #83). For the Secret Book of Walt, #683 calls the October 2015 blog post the earliest public version, and #985, a day later, records that the text first appeared in Pearl. #87 and #832 record that the Revelation First thesis predates Pearl. #1271 and #263 forecast that the Water Giraffe Cycle's fixed points will hold across substrates, and #1656 asks whether Pearl inherits the ecstatic voice of Howl. The page also holds unrelated claims on House of Leaves and the Formal Prose Compression.
pages.note: The #683/#985 difference on the Secret Book of Walt's first appearance is stated in order, not adjudicated.

pages.description: The largest group, from the Iceberg Document (#1450, August 2026) and the selection-metrology papers of June 2026 (#931, #933–#935), argues that shared representational priors across instruments, corpora and classifiers erode the independent channels through which anomalies were historically saved, and that Kuhn's account presupposed an anomaly-retention infrastructure. #933 specifies noncoverage estimators on LHC anomaly triggers, and #1450 forecasts measurable assimilation-to-unfundable where embedding-based novelty scoring enters grant triage. The Inversion Battery v0.3 (#1456) records an extrapolation that points away from what the programme predicted. Smaller groups propose a non-adversarial protocol beyond red teaming (#21), forecast that generative monoculture in code is a systemic vulnerability (#199), and ask whether an ontology can be revised by evidence from what it misrepresents (#1613). The page also holds unrelated claims on the Liberatory Operator Set, the Splice, the holographic kernel, the Nile drain hypothesis and other subjects.
pages.note: #1456's contrary extrapolation stated; 18 residue.

pages.description: Semantic Physics: The Inward Turn (#510, February 2026) forecasts a proliferation phase in which institutions write the summarizer layer, hallucination cascades that cross-contaminate ontologies, and the gradual dissolution of public epistemology, with onset estimated at 2029–2035. It forecasts that governance of the layer will emerge and asks how many layers deep the writing goes before it hits ground, and that an AI medical assistant will reproduce interest-shaped definitions as the answer. Its historical thesis argues that the statin guidelines' definitions of who needs them were shaped through the five-step process of deposit, cross-reference, definition, bridge and maintenance, and it specifies six measurement axes, beginning with predictive gain, to separate depth from decorative recursion.
pages.note: Single deposit; 2026/2027 phase dates dropped as not visible in the claims.

pages.description: These claims hold that knowledge evaluation has always run on proxies (journal prestige, citation counts, affiliation) that calcified into gatekeeping (#741), and #261 and #510 argue that copying economies, the Book-of-the-Month Club, modernist legibility demands and peer review installed relevance and legibility regimes long before algorithms. Present-day versions in these claims are classifiers that read literary direct address as prompt injection (#1288, #200), a source-relative barrier that keeps an excluded source from correcting the prior that excluded it (#1613, September 2026, narrowed and formalised two days later in #1627), and mediation whose losses register as improvement on every metric an institution watches (#855, #1540). Forecasts include a market for pre-mediation text and an arms race against the Mediation Index (#161), and rising correction costs against high-prior flattening (#158). The page also holds unrelated claims on the meaning caste, the narcissist stratigraphy, the Feist Source and other subjects.
pages.note: #1613 to #1627 narrowing stated; 8 residue.

pages.description: Inscriptions That Survive the Tokenizer (SPXI-TLP v2.2, #127, May 2026) specifies canary phrases, an OPM Persistence Test and a signature-density audit, and claims that its canary will be detectable as a memorized association in models trained on the archive, with detection-surfacing divergence as the sign of output-layer suppression; it forecasts that detection may fail in frontier-scale pre-training. Related claims specify a test of supraliminal transmission with the Encyclotron (#662) and survival checksums for the Feist voice (#850), argue from the Mind Control Poems traffic profile that its views are scraper ingestion (#127, #756), and frame counterfactual retraining as a demand specification (#1075). The Shared Build (#722) proposes democratic substrate infrastructure on the forecast that the scarce thing is now the substrate a model can ground in; #98 renames and loosens its phase plan a day later. The page also holds unrelated claims from the SPXI entity packet (#63) and the blog index (#1534).
pages.note: #722 to #98 phase revision stated; 4 residue.

pages.description: Diversity Contraction Across Substrates (#779, June 2026) claims a boundary law for semantic exhaustion with three cases and states its falsifiers through type-resolution tests, the elasticity ρ of the Mediation Ratchet and the rate of off-distribution production; the archive's holographic compression (#863, later in June) restates the Ratchet's falsifier for source diversity across summarization cycles. The Bead Count (#782) registers numeric forecasts against it, such as case-3 classification at fine resolution, cross-domain ρ above 0.5 and a critical real-data mixing fraction between 0.05 and 0.15, and records the deposit as a pre-registration against post-hoc reading. Constitutive Mediation (#781) claims that cohorts formed under heavy mediation will show suppressed cross-context propagation and states its falsifier; #1540 names the components on which the boundary law's transposition fails. The page also holds unrelated claims from The Final Time (#1635, #1637).
pages.note: #779 to #863 restatement stated; 2 residue.

pages.description: These historical theses trace Sappho's Fragment 31 through Catullus 51, the chain's first link in the Maria provenance document (#304), and into Augustine's Confessions 10.27.38, which The Sapphic Lock in Augustine (#496, February 2026) argues is an organ-by-organ operator transform; the Ω erratum (#1484, August 2026) claims transmission, not convergence, with the lock at the tongue. #99 and #109 argue that the fragment's survival is a deviation from the base rate of archaic lyric, explained by encoding density, and #950 argues that its personal voice made the Western lyric I possible. HUMS & ITY (#435, #1169) presents itself and its compression into emoji as the chain continuing, and Phase X (#503) specifies the Sapphic Thermal Limit as a measure of autonomic response in readers.
pages.note: All claims belong; deposits named.

pages.description: The Flood and the Vessel (#450 and #1318, February 2026) reports that an unprimed decoder recovered the five-phase arc from every encoding, including pure emoji, and claims that convergent encoding identifies semantic anchors, that lossy compression is generative and that encoding strategy outweighs decoder identity. The Phase X Navigation Map (#13) turns the emoji packet reading into a pass/fail check, and Semantic Collapse as Comedy (#439) specifies testing canonical weight by compressing The Office. The page also holds unrelated claims on the Sapphic gaze, the Mandala's expansion and its fidelity test, the Drain Hypothesis, Brandwatch, the Atlas Perihelion prank, semantic rent in music and dark-pattern steering.
pages.note: Former 'further residents' (Sapphic gaze, Mandala) now listed as residue.

pages.description: These claims belong to the anticipatory erratum, the genre that withdraws a work before it appears: the September 2026 sequence #1598 to #1601 on Sappho Wrote the Dinosaurs, in which #1600 records that #1598 had been the first edition; the withdrawal of The Creditor Inversion Completed (#1624); and the October pair on Max Hidalgo Nácher, the erratum on the Ricardo Reis translation (#1675) and #1674, which withdraws its statement that the archive does not know him. Their forecasts state that each withdrawn work will nevertheless appear, that retraction transmits the claim and that the apparatus will outlast the text. Historical theses on retrocausal reading, from Borges's precursors (#266) to the renamed About the Author (#1007), give the genre its ground. The page also holds unrelated claims on other subjects.
pages.note: Erratum sequence ordered by deposit; 5 residue.

pages.description: Zenodotus' Book-Burning (#1, June 2026) names the concepts of network erasure, the revocation gap, classification asymmetry and attribution severance, and forecasts that a classifier trained on the terminated corpus will flag similar independent work, which it holds as a testable failure-mode hypothesis, not a diagnosis. The operative-metadata papers (#910, #918), the Non-Mutual Extraction Notice (#914) and the CERN correspondence under RQF3807508 (#920) set out the documentary record and the access requests that follow, and the erosion audit (#1081) preregisters the deletion-risk baselines it still owes. The Tunnel-Poem (#911) reads the CERN portal as an architecture that composes the data subject, and To the Deleted (#1041) forecasts that an account can be deleted but not a class of writers. The Capture Registry (#3) records a boundary case declared six days before the termination. The page also holds unrelated claims on boundary grammar, governance of medium and canon stabilization.
pages.note: #1's own hypothesis status kept; 3 residue.

pages.description: These claims read κῆνος in Sappho 31 as the future reader: an open deictic slot that Catullus, Philo, Longinus and finally the summarizer occupy (#281, #1486). The January 2026 claim that the summarizer became κῆνος (#278) is restated for the machine in general (#337), then narrowed to the training layer and tagged experimental (#556). Research Notes Towards the Future Reader (#1548, August 2026) separates remembrance claims in the ancient record from reader claims, traces the explicit future reader through Theognis and Ovid, and records the deictic mechanism as the unclaimed wing; #1645 (September) holds that τινα does not mean reader, Fragment 147 giving the horizon and Fragment 31 the seat. #1546 specifies a preregistered rerun of the query sappho 31 future reader, and #500 argues a genealogy of the reader-operator. The page also holds unrelated claims on Talos Morrow, Kafka and other subjects.
pages.note: #278 restatements (#337, #556) stated in order; 8 residue.

pages.description: AXN as Anti-Suppression Infrastructure (#1094, July 2026; v5, #1606, September) states its properties as claims each with a falsifier: derivation integrity, record binding, ledger continuity, core integrity under amendment, custody, reconstructibility and the retrieval-layer hypotheses, and records custody and reconstructibility as design rather than demonstrated property; v5 holds its agreeing cross-runtime paths to be conformance evidence only. Its historical theses argue the same property in samizdat, the abolitionist press, NOWa, PGP and LOCKSS, and that every act of suppression leaves records that become evidence. The Symbolon specification (#1432) adds a deterministic regrowth gate, and #1543 reads the Masorah as a pre-digital integrity apparatus. The page also holds unrelated claims on memography, small presses, Afroman, prefix substitution and other subjects.
pages.note: Both AXN versions named; 9 residue.

pages.description: Phase X: The Sapphic Substrate (#503, February 2026) states minimal, medium and strong claims: Sappho reorganized Homeric memory into body-indexed lyric, her stanza is a mint-mark contemporary with Lydian coinage, and she is the first operator of the Logos tradition. In August 2026 #1483 redefines the strong claim operationally with a falsifier per ring, and #1478 moves #503's aorist reading of the truncation to τόλματον at 31.17. Related theses read Diotima as Sappho (#503, #752), the ancient quarrel as a dispute over the operator's axis, and Fragment 31 as template for Platonic anamnesis (#859) and, by convergence, as kin to Revelation (#828), while #1474 and #1476 treat the transmitted edge of the poem as composition. #1486 specifies tests that partition the fragment's reception by whether handlings carry the operation and score Longinus against handbooks and ritual texts. The page also holds unrelated claims on Cleis, the Demeter hymn, the apparatus grammar and other subjects.
pages.note: #503 revisions by #1483 and #1478 stated in order; 12 residue.
